evidence:
Workbook #32: 'Each criterion is a concrete, browser-observable outcome with durable evidence and distinctive probes. Reports every instance.' Skill reference #32 defect list: 'looks right', a source read, a response-shape assertion with no state change, or a probe that leaves no trace. No Internal annotation exists for #32.

WHAT IS GOOD (all 3 gate/scored binary dimensions, 47 binary criteria + 5 Likert): every binary criterion names a concrete stage/place/count/text/focus outcome with explicit fail conditions; refusals are paired with 'nothing changed' readbacks and named positive controls (e.g. functional/judge.toml hro_job_open, hro_reject_hired, hro_undo_full, hro_anonymous 'A signed-in success of each is the control'); independent-context recipe for shared state is spelled out (functional/prompt.md:11; constraints/prompt.md:9); focus/scroll are made measurable (document.activeElement in hro_refused_put_back and hro_pol_live_board; getBoundingClientRect().top in hro_pol_earlier_place); live timing has a deterministic cut-off ('accept what is present at the first snapshot at or after 15 seconds', functional/prompt.md:45); failed-send has a traceful probe (abort exactly one request, 'sent once', polish/judge.toml hro_pol_failed_send); restart uses restart_app with explicit before/after records (functional/prompt.md:49, hro_restart). No criterion asks for a source read; hro_anonymous's 401 is a public rule (hireops_rules.md §1) and is paired with 'nothing is returned or changed'. Visual Likert rows are judgement-by-design with 5 described anchors (shipped format, check 41 territory) and are not counted as 'looks right' instances. Gates (hro_gate_render, hro_gate_shared) are concrete and require a real write plus independent-context readback.

INSTANCES FOUND (every instance):

(1) [P2, main] Capacity and bulk all-or-none probes are not distinctive between server enforcement and client-only pre-validation. functional/prompt.md:23 permits replay only 'Where the UI does not offer an action that a step says to try'; prompt.md:17 'Request replays are permitted only where a protocol says so'. Protocol L (prompt.md:29) 'Move E to Screen and try Screen→Interview: refused' and protocol B (prompt.md:33) steps (5) 'Select V and Z and try Interview ... refused' and (7) 'Select V, W, X and try Interview (3 into 2 places): refused' are therefore satisfied by a UI-level refusal whenever the UI offers the control and refuses it locally. Affected criteria: hro_interview_full (w1.5, judge.toml:104-111), hro_bulk_all_or_none (w2, :212-219), hro_bulk_places (w1.5, :221-228); the same applies to the skip leg of hro_move_one_stage (w1.5, :50-57) when the skip is offered but locally refused. hireops_rules.md §3 says 'A move that would put more cards into Interview than there are places is refused' and 'If any card fails, none of them moves', and the brief's core concern is several people acting at once (instruction.md:1), so a client-side-only check is a broken product (two users with stale boards overfill Interview), yet no criterion forces the server-side probe for a plain move or bulk set. The template's rule 'A hidden, missing or disabled control is not enforcement: the matching forged request must also be refused' (template functional/prompt.md:44-45) is not carried into this prompt. Only undo-into-full (hro_undo_full) and the stale move (hro_stale_refused) necessarily hit the server.

(2) [P2] hro_refused_put_back (w2, judge.toml:131-138) is only decidable if the UI actually sends the over-capacity move. A conforming UI that disables or omits Screen→Interview while Interview shows '2 of 2' (not forbidden by instruction.md or hireops_rules.md) produces no 'page that made the refused full-Interview move'; the prompt's fallback is a page.evaluate replay (prompt.md:23), which cannot exhibit UI put-back or focus. The criterion text gives no verdict rule for this case, so the judge must guess (0 for a conforming app, or 1 with nothing observed). The golden happens to send the move (board.js:170/197/203 refocus after server refusal), so the golden is unaffected; alternative conforming apps are at risk.

(3) [P3] hro_undo_once (w1, judge.toml:248-255) contains the leg '(and a repeated undo request is refused)', but protocol B step (4) (prompt.md:33) only says 'no undo is offered any more' and contains no 'try' step, while prompt.md:17 forbids replays except where a protocol says so. The leg is either unexercisable (judge must skip or zero it) or invites an unauthorized replay; inconsistent decision rule.

(4) [P3, latent] hro_unread_counts (w2, judge.toml:329-336) hard-codes 'Mei Lin starts with 2 unread on Tomas Varga's Data Analyst conversation', while the same prompt says 'never rely on starting counts' (prompt.md:15) and 'Earlier reviews may have added ... messages'. Seed check: APP-201 has 3 messages (Mei Lin, Tomas, Tomas) and Mei's read marker is 1 → 2 is correct at seed. But the scored suite runs functional/polish/visual on one shared DB (test.sh:224, one rewardkit run over /tests/scored) and polish rows let Rafael send 'in a conversation' (hro_pol_failed_send) and make Mei Lin 'open that conversation' (hro_pol_session_resume) without naming which; if polish ran first and picked APP-201, Mei's starting count would no longer be 2 and a correct app would fail. Dimension order inside rewardkit is not established by any task file I read; if functional runs first (alphabetical), the instance does not trigger. Not measured.

(5) [Note, no defect] hro_bulk_move 'Fails if they move one by one with separate results' is the vaguest wording among the binary rows, but the paired observable (one action; one undo restores all three, hro_undo_restores) makes it decidable.

RUNTIME: raw-evidence-index.json states 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent'; the scripted golden driver 'does not walk every Functional criterion as the judge would'. No judge run exercises these probes, so instances (1)-(4) are source-derived and NOT EXERCISED at runtime.
counterexample: Broken app that passes: the board client checks Interview capacity and stage-skips (single and bulk) against its locally loaded board and shows 'Interview is full (2 of 2)' / 'Z would skip a stage' without sending anything; the server's move endpoint accepts any one-stage-or-more move with no capacity check and processes bulk sets card by card. Under protocols L and B the judge sees UI refusals with unchanged cards, never replays (prompt.md:23 only allows replay when the action is not offered), and awards hro_interview_full, hro_bulk_all_or_none, hro_bulk_places (and the skip leg of hro_move_one_stage) = 6.5 weight units, although two recruiters with stale boards can overfill Interview. Conforming app that may fail: a UI that disables Screen→Interview while Interview is full never produces a refused move on the page, so hro_refused_put_back (w2) has nothing to observe and is likely scored 0.
suggested_fix: In protocols L and B, after each UI refusal (or non-offer), require replaying the captured successful move/bulk request with the over-capacity or skipping card(s) in Rafael's session and require server refusal plus unchanged readback in hro_interview_full, hro_bulk_all_or_none, hro_bulk_places and hro_move_one_stage; make hro_refused_put_back use a refusal the client cannot pre-empt (e.g. the stale move of protocol C made through the UI, or state an explicit verdict when the UI pre-disables the move); add an explicit replay step for the repeated undo in protocol B(4) or drop that leg; and either name a conversation for the polish draft/send rows other than APP-201 or measure Mei's baseline relative to the start of U instead of hard-coding 2.
